### Insights and directions

**Starting point.** (1) Sampled training margins are generally positive, yet Electronics has a 7.15% negative-beats-positive rate. This motivates testing stronger competition without assuming training separation predicts validation HR@10. (2) Logit dispersion differs across datasets. Raw margins therefore require score-scale context when comparing objectives. (3) Qualitative feedback identifies broad associations and redundant alternatives. These observations motivate investigating ranking specificity, but do not establish that loss choice causes those failures.

**Related work.** (1) Di Teodoro et al. show that single-negative categorical cross-entropy equals BPR and provide favorable worst-case bounds for BCE [1]. Softmax superiority must therefore remain a hypothesis. (2) Scaled cross-entropy and logQ studies identify normalization and sampling treatment as consequential [2,3]. Negative count, weighting, and candidate eligibility need explicit controls. (3) Sequentiality audits question whether accuracy demonstrates long-history reasoning [4]. An objective improvement would establish a ranking result, without establishing better intent understanding.

### Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Atomic intervention | Question |
|---|---|---|
| Competition | BCE-1 versus BCE-32 | Does additional negative exposure help? |
| Objective | BCE-32 versus softmax-32 | Does coupled competition help? |
| Mechanism | Fixed-pool gradient audit | Which negatives receive learning signal? |

Scores below are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Matched-negative objective comparison: 3/8/3.** Originality: isolates confounds, but uses established objectives. Potential: yields actionable evidence, but may be benchmark-specific. Difficulty: changes only training loss, but matching samplers and checkpoints requires care.
2. **BCE negative-count increase alone: 2/6/2.** Originality: clean exposure intervention, but conventional. Potential: inexpensive improvement candidate, but may amplify popularity effects. Difficulty: straightforward vectorization, but increases memory and compute.
3. **Fixed-pool gradient concentration audit: 5/6/4.** Originality: connects objective differences to negative allocation, but remains descriptive. Potential: guides subsequent sampling research, but cannot establish generalization. Difficulty: local logit derivatives are simple, but tied-embedding attribution is harder.

### Selected idea: matched-negative objective comparison

At 10% progress, prioritize idea 1. Keep four independent baseline SASRec models and compare BCE-1, balanced BCE-32, and softmax-32 using identical initial weights, minibatch order, and eligible negative pools. BCE-1 uses one predetermined pool member; BCE-32 averages its negative term so negative count does not multiply its weight. Softmax uses temperature 1 and no additional sampling correction; it is a restricted-candidate objective.

```python
p, n = score_positive(h), score_negatives(h, pool32)
BCE1  = softplus(-p) + softplus(n[:, 0])
BCE32 = softplus(-p) + softplus(n).mean(-1)
SM32  = logsumexp(cat([p[:, None], n]), -1) - p
loss = selected_loss.mean()  # valid positions only
```

Preserve seeds, splits, routing, environment epoch defaults, diagnostic interfaces, and predictor export parity. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; report per-category results and compute cost. Predeclare checkpoint rules and cap aggregate training and diagnostics at 43,200 GPU-seconds. Retain twenty-user recommendation audits as auxiliary evidence; no improvement is established beforehand.

References: [1] arXiv:2411.07770; [2] arXiv:2408.14238; [3] arXiv:2507.09331; [4] arXiv:2408.12008.

idea.description: Compare unchanged four-dataset SASRec trained with BCE-1, balanced BCE-32, and restricted-candidate softmax-32, using matched initialization, training examples, and negative pools.
idea.motivation: Current diagnostics demonstrate separation from sampled training negatives but do not establish validation ranking quality. Matching negative exposure between BCE-32 and softmax-32 helps distinguish objective effects from the benefit of encountering more negatives.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, unchanged splits, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior (default 200). Sample 32 unique eligible nonpadding negatives per valid prediction position under the baseline training eligibility policy, without consulting validation or test labels. Reuse identical pools for BCE-32 and softmax-32; BCE-1 receives a predetermined member. If fewer than 32 eligible items exist, use the available unique items and mask unused slots in both objectives. Match initial model states, minibatch order, optimizer settings, and checkpoint opportunities; use separate random generators for negatives and diagnostics. Define BCE as positive softplus plus mean negative softplus, preserving the baseline convention if equivalent and documenting any difference. Softmax uses temperature 1 and no logQ correction; do not claim an unbiased full-catalog likelihood. Use valid-position means and preserve baseline regularization consistently. Bound compute before launching controls; stop at the aggregate budget even if the planned comparison remains incomplete. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), metric definitions, and the actual trained module through view.model. Existing one-negative margin probes remain comparable auxiliary measurements; mark architecture-specific residual probes inapplicable. Preserve compatibility fields without fabricating unavailable metadata or reviews. Keep the unchanged architecture in the predictor writer, save objective and sampler configuration beneath the trial directory, and verify exported inference scores and routing. Select only through the pinned macro validation HR@10 with predeclared checkpoint and tie rules. Preserve full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five training users per category; qualitative audits cannot substitute for benchmark selection.

originality.positive: The matched-pool design explicitly separates negative exposure from objective coupling in this task.
originality.negative: BCE, sampled softmax, and controlled negative-count comparisons are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: A clear objective comparison can guide subsequent sampling and gradient-allocation research across all four datasets.
future_potential.negative: Any result may depend on the fixed sampled evaluation, optimizer settings, and available search budget.

code_difficulty.positive: The architecture and inference contract remain unchanged; implementation centers on sampling and vectorized losses.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible pools, explicit loss weighting, bounded memory, and fair checkpoint selection require careful integration.

related_work.title: Di Teodoro et al.: analysis of recommendation losses under negative sampling
contributions: The supplied search summary reports equivalence between single-negative categorical cross-entropy and BPR.
Provides theoretical motivation for retaining BCE as a serious control.
limitations: Worst-case ranking bounds do not determine empirical macro validation HR@10 in this task.

related_work.title: Scaled cross-entropy
contributions: The supplied summary reports benefits from increasing the sampled normalizing term, motivating explicit normalization controls.
limitations: Reported benefits do not establish that ordinary softmax-32 will outperform balanced BCE-32 here.

related_work.title: RecSys 2025 work on logQ correction
contributions: Distinguishes deterministically included positives from sampled negatives and highlights consequences for gradient weighting.
limitations: Correction choices depend on the sampling scheme and intended objective; they should not be added without specifying both.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Compares original and shuffled interaction sequences across multiple datasets, motivating caution about claims of temporal reasoning.
limitations: Sequentiality findings do not identify the best training objective for these four Amazon datasets.
